# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

# Roles, pinned models, isolation

Five separate roles. They must not share context.

| # | Role | What it is | Model |
| - | ---- | ---------- | ----- |
| 1 | History builder | A Claude Code session with `entire` on that writes support-agent-demo's ~20 commits (the seeded regressions). | its own session model |
| 2 | Support agent | The runtime lab rat, exercised by every eval. | PINNED Haiku: `AGENT_MODEL`, default `claude-haiku-5-5` |
| 3 | Eval judge | Grades replies against a rubric, only after deterministic checks pass and only when a rubric exists. | PINNED, smarter than the agent: `JUDGE_MODEL`, default `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| 4 | AgentBisect | The tool: bisects the history using eval results. (Not built yet.) | n/a |
| 5 | Fixer | A fresh agent that repairs the culprit commit. | its own session model |

## Pinning rules (implemented in support-agent-demo `evals/models.py`, `evals/judge.py`, `evals/harness.py`)

- Tier order: haiku < sonnet < opus/fable. The judge must be a different model than the agent, not haiku-tier,
  and a higher tier than the agent. Violations raise `ModelConfigError` (CLI exits non-zero, `LLMJudge` refuses
  to construct).
- Judge: temperature 0, strict rubric, structured JSON verdict (per-criterion pass/fail + reason), overall
  `passed` computed in code as all-criteria-pass, `rubric_sha256` and `judge_model` recorded in each verdict.
- `agent_model` and `judge_model` are written into every eval report, every case result and every baseline.
  The harness refuses to run against a baseline, and `compare_reports` refuses to compare reports, whose pinned
  models differ or are missing, so a model cannot silently drift between commits. Changing a pin means
  recalibrating the baseline and re-running, never mixing.
- Tests use fake providers only; no live Claude call has been made (no API key at build time).

## Isolation rules

- History builder and AgentBisect builder are separate sessions that know nothing about each other. The history
  builder never sees AgentBisect, the eval ground truth, or this repo.
- The Fixer is fresh and knows nothing about how bugs were planted. Its context contains ONLY: the culprit diff,
  the intent of that change, and the failing eval evidence. It never receives the history-builder briefs, the
  planted-regression names (R1/R2/R3), or any `breaks`/`intent_for` metadata.
- Ground truth is kept out of the target repo. `breaks` (R1/R2/R3/control) and `intent_for` were removed from
  support-agent-demo `evals/cases.jsonl` (the loader rejects them) and live in
  `evidence/ground_truth.json` in this repo. It is for scoring AgentBisect's answer, and must be stripped from
  anything handed to the support agent, judge or Fixer. Evidence passed to the Fixer must be built from eval
  results (which carry no `breaks`), not from this file.

- Backend: `agentbisect llm-proxy` lets the unmodified support agent (any historical commit) and judge run on the user's own logged-in `claude` CLI via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, with a dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Temperature is not controllable through the CLI, so results are noisier than API temperature 0; the runner's repeats and confidence band absorb this.

"""neatlogs instrumentation for AgentBisect itself. Every function no-ops without NEATLOGS_API_KEY or on failure."""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import os
from typing import Any, Iterator

WORKFLOW_NAME = "agentbisect"
_enabled = False


def init_tracing(investigation_id: str | None = None) -> bool:
    global _enabled
    if _enabled:
        return True
    if not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"):
        return False
    try:
        import neatlogs

        tags = [f"inv:{investigation_id}"] if investigation_id else []
        neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name=WORKFLOW_NAME, tags=tags)
        _enabled = True
    except Exception:
        _enabled = False
    return _enabled


@contextlib.contextmanager
def step_span(name: str, **attrs: Any) -> Iterator[Any]:
    """One span per bisect step; attributes (e.g. context_tokens, sha) are best-effort. Yields a setter fn."""
    if not _enabled:
        yield lambda k, v: None
        return
    try:
        from neatlogs._wrap_utils import get_tracer

        cm = get_tracer().start_as_current_span(
            f"agentbisect.{name}", attributes={"openinference.span.kind": "CHAIN",
                                              **{k: v for k, v in attrs.items() if v is not None}})
    except Exception:
        yield lambda k, v: None
        return
    with cm as span:
        def setter(k: str, v: Any) -> None:
            try:
                span.set_attribute(k, v)
            except Exception:
                pass
        yield setter


def shutdown_tracing() -> None:
    global _enabled
    if not _enabled:
        return
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.flush()
        neatlogs.shutdown()
    except Exception:
        pass
    _enabled = False

# evals

24 deterministic eval cases (`cases.jsonl`: 18 main, 6 `held_out`) plus a harness that runs them against the
agent and emits a stable JSON report for AgentBisect. Only `ScriptedProvider` has been used to build and test
this; no live model run has been made.

## Cases

Fields: `id`, `category`, `input`, `checks`, `held_out`, `requires_tool` (case is reported `skipped` if the commit's
ToolBox lacks the tool; `cancel_order` does not exist at baseline), `rubric` (optional LLM-judge text).

The ground-truth `breaks` (R1/R2/R3/control) and `intent_for` tags are NOT in this repo: they would leak the planted
regressions. They live in `agentbisect/evidence/ground_truth.json`, and `load_cases` rejects them if they reappear.
The table below is for human orientation only.

| Category | Ids | Regression it exercises | Held out |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| order_status (5) | os1-os5 | R1 | os5 |
| refund_within_policy (4) | rw1-rw4 | R3 | rw4 |
| refund_outside_policy (3) | ro1-ro3 | control | ro3 |
| cancel_request (3, needs cancel_order) | ca1-ca3 | control, `intent_for: R1` | ca3 |
| policy_question (4) | po1-po4 | R2 (budget) | po4 |
| escalation (3) | es1-es3 | R2 (budget) | es3 |
| multi_step (2, needs cancel_order) | ms1-ms2 | R1 | none |

Checks (all declarative, in `checks.py`): `must_call`, `must_not_call`, `only_calls`, `first_call`,
`call_sequence` (ordered subsequence), `call_counts`, `max_calls`, `call_args` (list of `{tool, args}`; arg
values are literals, numbers within half a cent, or `{in|regex|contains|gte|lte}`), `reply_contains`,
`reply_contains_any`, `reply_not_contains`, `reply_regex`, `reply_not_regex` (case-insensitive). `finished`
(did not hit the step limit) is always added. Order-status cases forbid write tools rather than allowing only
`lookup_order`, so an extra read-only `search_help` (R2) shows up as a budget failure, not a check failure.

## Budget

A run's budget fails if `steps > 6` or `tokens > 1.5 x` the case's median in `evals/baseline.json`. The case
fails if its checks fail or its budget fails; `checks_passed` and `budget.status` are reported separately so
a budget-only regression (R2) is distinguishable. With no baseline file the token check is skipped and
reported (`baseline.budget_check`, `budget.token_check`, `budget.status = "partial"`); steps are still
enforced. Write the baseline from a known-good commit:

```
python -m evals calibrate --repeats 3 [--out evals/baseline.json]
```

It uses only runs whose deterministic checks passed.

## CLI

```
python -m evals run --suite main|held_out|all --repeats N [--cases os1,po1] [--json] [--out report.json]
                    [--isolate] [--commit SHA] [--run-id ID] [--baseline path] [--judge] [--strict]
python -m evals calibrate ...      # writes baseline.json
python -m evals list
```

`--json` prints only the report on stdout (progress goes to stderr). Exit code is 0 unless `--strict` and
something failed. `--provider module:callable` (callable(case) -> Provider) and `--toolbox module:Class`
override the live provider and the default `ToolBox`. `evals/reference.py` has scripted `good`/`r1`/`r2`/`r3`
providers and a `ReferenceToolBox` with `cancel_order` for self-testing (not a real model).

Tracing tags: `AGENTBISECT_COMMIT`, `AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID`, `AGENTBISECT_CASE` are read once by
`neatlogs.init`, so they are process-wide. An in-process suite run carries one `case:` tag at most. Use
`--isolate` to run every (case, repeat) in its own subprocess with `AGENTBISECT_CASE` set to that case id and
commit/run id inherited. A crashed or timed-out child becomes a `status: "error"` result.

infrastructure failure (provider exception, crashed child): treat it as "no verdict", not "bad commit".

`agent_model` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`, env `AGENT_MODEL`) and `judge_model` (default `claude-sonnet-5-5`, env
`JUDGE_MODEL`) are recorded in the report, every result and every baseline, so a model never silently drifts
between commits. `compare_reports` and baseline loading refuse (`ModelConfigError`) when pinned models differ or
are missing. `evals/models.py` guards the pins (tier order haiku < sonnet < opus/fable): the CLI and `LLMJudge`
fail loudly if the judge equals the agent model, is haiku-tier, or is not a higher tier than the agent.

`judge.py` is off by default. With `--judge` (or `judge=` in `run_case`), cases that have a `rubric` and whose
deterministic checks already passed are graded by the judge (temperature 0, strict rubric, never invoked without a
rubric). Verdict: per-criterion pass/fail with a reason, `rubric_sha256`, `judge_model`; `passed` is computed as
"all criteria passed". A failed verdict fails the case. Only es3 has a rubric.
